articles.title: Two days of rain bring Delhi’s AQI down to 60; minister credits ‘targeted action’ for cleaner air
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: After two days of rainfall brought considerable relief from pollution in the national capital, Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Friday
articles.body: NEW DELHI: After two days of rainfall brought considerable relief from pollution in the national capital, Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Friday credited the government’s “targeted action” and public participation for the improvement in air quality, even as a report pointed to the significant role played by favourable weather conditions.Sirsa shared visuals of India Gate on X, highlighting an AQI reading of 93 and describing it as “Satisfactory”. He said the improvement showed that targeted action was producing results."Seeing visuals of India Gate with a 'Satisfactory' AQI of 93 is proof that targeted action brings real results. Under the leadership of CM Rekha Gupta, our government is working round the clock on anti-pollution measures, but real change happens when governance is backed by strong Jan Bhagidari. A huge thank you to the people of Delhi for their active participation in our mission for clean air. Let’s keep working together for a healthier, greener Delhi!!" Sirsa posted on X.However, Delhi's air quality improvement has coincided with an unusually wet October.As per news agency PTI, the city recorded an average AQI of 167 this month, its lowest October average since 2015, according to an analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).The AQI stood at 60 on Friday, making it the cleanest October day since October 10, 2022, when it was recorded at 44. The highest AQI recorded this month was 245, the lowest monthly peak since 2015.As per the PTI report, Delhi received 61.4mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending 8.30am on Friday, making it the wettest October day in four years and the sixth wettest October day since 1951. The city recorded cumulative rainfall of 123.3mm till 8.30am on Friday, more than eight times its monthly normal of 15.1mm.The improvement in air quality comes against the backdrop of a series of unusually wet days. The city recorded five days of 'poor' air quality, three 'satisfactory' days and 22 'moderate' days in October so far. Air quality entered the 'poor' category on October 21, when the AQI rose to 245.Manoj Kumar of CREA pointed to the influence of weather conditions while assessing the improvement in pollution levels."Delhi recorded a relatively lower average AQI in October 2026 compared with previous Octobers, although it remained 1.5 times higher than the average AQI for September 2026."AQI was already relatively low before GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan) was imposed, and declined to 60 on October 30, coinciding with 61.4 mm of rainfall at Safdarjung. This highlights the importance of accounting for meteorological influences before attributing improvements in air quality to GRAP measures."Delhi's average AQI in October was 167 this year, compared with 223 in 2025, 234 in 2024, 219 in 2023, 210 in 2022 and 264 in 2015. Its average AQI between January and October stood at 168, the lowest for the period since 2020, when it was 156.The capital also recorded its wettest October in four years, with 123.3 mm of rainfall till Friday morning. It was also the coldest October day in terms of maximum temperature since 1951, with the maximum temperature at Safdarjung settling at 20.7 degrees Celsius on Friday.The data highlights the role of rainfall and other meteorological conditions in the recent improvement in Delhi's air quality, even as the government continues to highlight its anti-pollution measures.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: A silver airship-shaped cabin became one of Scotland's most unusual holiday rentals; now AirShip 002 and two neighbouring retreats, a business grossing around £100,000 a year, are listed for over £750,000
articles.summary: A striking silver cabin shaped like an airship has become one of Scotland’s most recognisable holiday rentals, and now the business behind it is on the
articles.body: A striking silver cabin shaped like an airship has become one of Scotland’s most recognisable holiday rentals, and now the business behind it is on the market. AirShip 002, along with two neighbouring retreats at Druim Na Cracaig on the Morvern Peninsula near Oban, has been listed by Savills for offers over £750,000. The collection of architecturally designed properties generates around £100,000 in gross annual income and has attracted guests from around the world, including visitors from Japan. The sale offers more than a distinctive place to stay. It includes a proven hospitality business, a four-acre elevated coastal site, and three properties that have become destinations in their own right. According to The Scotsman, AirShip 002 has earned international attention for its curved aluminium form, dragonfly windows, and dramatic views over the Sound of Mull, while the wider portfolio has appeared on television programs and regularly features in lists of Britain’s most unusual holiday homes. Read more details about it here:The cabin that looks like an AirshipAirShip 002 was designed by architect Roderick James and designer Amanda Markham as a modern interpretation of a streamlined airship. Its aluminium-clad exterior, curved silhouette, and distinctive dragonfly windows give it the appearance of a futuristic vessel resting above the Scottish coastline. The cabin sits in a remote setting with panoramic sea views toward the Ardnamurchan Peninsula and across the Sound of Mull.The unusual design has made AirShip 002 one of the most wish-listed Airbnb properties in the United Kingdom. Savills describes it as an internationally recognised retreat with a large collection of five-star guest reviews and a loyal following. Its appeal lies not only in its appearance, but in the sense of escape it offers: a compact, carefully designed cabin set within one of Scotland’s most dramatic coastal landscapes.The cabin’s success inspired the creation of two additional retreats. The PilotHouse is a two-storey hideaway with an elliptical form and a raised first floor living space designed to maximize views toward Tobermory and the open sea. The Captain’s Cabin is a smaller, nautically inspired escape with a private rooftop viewing balcony, a cosy salon, a pantry kitchen, a double bedroom, and a shower room.A business with a proven incomeThe Druim Na Cracaig portfolio is being sold as an established holiday rental business rather than simply a collection of unusual buildings. Savills says the three retreats have produced a stable annual gross turnover of about £100,000 over the past four years. Owner Roderick James told The Scotsman that the lets require relatively little time to operate while continuing to attract international guests.The listing includes The Old Chapel, a two-bedroom owner’s or housekeeper’s residence beneath the Captain’s Cabin. It provides a practical base for managing the business while preserving guests’ privacy and independence. The four-acre site also includes extensive parking, storage, outbuildings, and workshop space, making it suitable for someone who wants to continue running the retreats as a hospitality operation.The properties have been designed with comfort and sustainability in mind. Savills highlights features such as high levels of insulation, underfloor heating, triple glazing, renewable electricity, and wood-burning stoves. Those details help make the cabins usable throughout the year, extending their appeal beyond the summer season and supporting the business’s consistent income.Why the retreats became famousAirShip 002 and its neighbours have appeared on television shows including Scotland’s Great Escapes and Alan Cumming’s Paradise Homes. They have also regularly appeared in media roundups of the most offbeat and distinctive holiday rentals in Britain. That exposure has helped turn the properties into a recognizable brand, with guests seeking them out specifically for the experience of staying somewhere truly different.The location adds to the appeal. Druim Na Cracaig is set on the Morvern Peninsula near Drimnin and Oban, a remote part of Scotland’s west coast known for sea views, quiet landscapes, and access to the Sound of Mull, as per the reports. Guests can look toward Tobermory and the distant mountains, making the retreats attractive to travellers seeking both architectural novelty and a genuine escape from busy city life.Savills property agent Iona Conn said few hospitality businesses combine imaginative architecture, proven commercial success, and such a captivating setting, as per The Scotsman. She described the portfolio as a rare opportunity to acquire an internationally recognized tourism business with an established income stream in one of the country’s most spectacular coastal locations.A Legacy Beyond Holiday LetsFor Roderick James, the retreats have also supported a wider purpose. A former architect specializing in oak-framed buildings, James designed new timber roofs for the Great Hall at Stirling Castle and Windsor Castle following the fire. He later became involved in social projects that build homes where they are needed most and teach project management and trade skills to disadvantaged young people and ex-offenders.Income from the holiday lets has helped support that charitable work. James has built at least 15 homes on the Morvern Peninsula, and a project to build cabins in Rwanda is also underway. He said sharing the special place with visitors from around the world has been hugely rewarding, and the sale now offers someone else the chance to continue that story.For buyers, the listing represents an unusual combination of lifestyle, architecture, and business. AirShip 002 may look like a silver airship floating above the coast, but behind its memorable design is a functioning holiday rental operation with a loyal audience and a steady income. At offers over £750,000, the next owner will inherit not just three distinctive cabins, but one of Scotland’s most recognizable small-scale hospitality brands.You use AI every day. articles.title: A UK woman claimed she could not walk, drive or work because of hip pain, but investigators found she was running a body-piercing business and working for other clients
articles.summary: A UK woman who claimed that hip pain left her unable to walk, drive or work has been ordered to pay more than £6,000 after admitting to fraudulently
articles.body: A UK woman who claimed that hip pain left her unable to walk, drive or work has been ordered to pay more than £6,000 after admitting to fraudulently claiming Statutory Sick Pay while working for other clients and running her own body-piercing business. Claire Hopkinson, a resident of Telford, Shropshire, submitted false medical fitness certificates, WhatsApp messages and emails to support her claims that she could not perform her duties as a personal carer. However, an investigation by Telford & Wrekin Council uncovered evidence that she was working as a personal assistant for two other individuals through a private care company. Investigators also found that she had fabricated claims about hospital stays and undergoing a hip replacement operation. She pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation on December 1, 2025.How the sick pay fraud was uncoveredAccording to Telford & Wrekin Council, Hopkinson fraudulently claimed Statutory Sick Pay between March 28, 2024, and October 28, 2024, while employed as a privately employed personal carer.During this period, she submitted medical fitness certificates, commonly known as fit notes, alongside WhatsApp messages and emails claiming that hip pain prevented her from working.She alleged that she could not walk, drive or perform her duties as a personal assistant. However, investigators discovered that she was working for two other individuals through a private care company while also operating her own local body-piercing business.The investigation also uncovered false claims about hospital stays and a hip replacement operation. The council said the medical events she described had been fabricated.Hopkinson received £3,261.65 in Statutory Sick Pay to which she was not entitled, according to the council's investigation.She fabricated hospital stays and a hip replacement operationThe investigation found that Hopkinson had gone beyond claiming that she was unable to work because of hip pain.According to the council, she fabricated accounts of hospital stays and claimed to have undergone a hip replacement operation. These claims were found to be false during the investigation.Her medical fitness certificates and electronic communications formed part of the evidence examined by investigators.The case ultimately led to her admitting to fraud by false representation. The council said the court highlighted the seriousness of the offence, including the extent of her attempts to cover up her actions.The authority has not published further details about the medical documents, the precise investigative methods used or how the false claims were independently verified.How much money did she have to pay?Hopkinson received £3,261.65 in Statutory Sick Pay through the fraudulent claims. Following her guilty plea, the court ordered her to pay a fine and costs totalling £2,814.She was also required to repay the falsely claimed sick pay directly to Telford & Wrekin Council.The combined amount exceeds £6,000, according to the authority.The financial consequences therefore include both the repayment of the money she received and the additional fine and court costs. The council's announcement does not confirm whether the full amount has already been repaid.She pleaded guilty to fraud by false representationHopkinson was interviewed under caution by council officers during the investigation and eventually admitted to the deception.On December 1, 2025, she pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation at court.The case was subsequently publicised by Telford & Wrekin Council on December 16, 2025, as part of its efforts to highlight action against fraud involving public funds.The council did not report a prison sentence in its announcement. Instead, it detailed the financial orders imposed following her guilty plea and confirmed that she was repaying the sick pay directly to the authority.Council says fraud diverts resources from those who need supportCouncillor Richard Overton, deputy leader of Telford & Wrekin Council and cabinet member for highways, housing and enforcement, said the case demonstrated the authority's commitment to tackling fraud and protecting public funds.He said fraudulent claims undermine trust and divert resources away from people who genuinely need support.The council also encouraged residents to report suspected fraud so that public money could be safeguarded and used to support those who need it.Hopkinson's case formed part of the authority's wider enforcement efforts to investigate suspected fraud and pursue action where wrongdoing is established.What is Statutory Sick Pay in the UK?Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a payment available to eligible employees who are unable to work because of illness. It is distinct from disability benefits and other forms of financial assistance.In Hopkinson's case, the fraud involved claiming SSP while allegedly being unable to work as a personal carer, despite undertaking other paid work and operating a business.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kate Winslet reads ‘Room on the Broom’ for children during the Halloween season, adding its 104th read-aloud to Storyline Online’s free literacy library
articles.summary: “The witch had a cat, and a hat that was black...” Kate Winslet’s voice rises and falls with the rhythm, turning each line into a visual as she reads
articles.body: “The witch had a cat, and a hat that was black...” Kate Winslet’s voice rises and falls with the rhythm, turning each line into a visual as she reads Julia Donaldson’s ‘Room on the Broom’. She does not rush. Rather, she lets the beat carry the story. The Academy Award-winning actor reads Room on the Broom in the latest video from Storyline Online, the children’s literacy programme that is free to watch at any hour. The read-aloud went live earlier this month on StorylineOnline.net and on the programme’s YouTube channel, just as the Halloween season gets underway.‘Room on the Broom’Written by Julia Donaldson and illustrated by Axel Scheffler, ‘Room on the Broom’ follows a friendly witch and her cat as they fly through the sky. When the wind blows away the witch’s hat, broom and wand, a helpful dog, bird and frog retrieve her belongings. In return, each of them asks for just one thing: a ride on the broom. The witch agrees and makes room for each new friend. However, the broom cannot hold the growing group of passengers and eventually snaps in two. The passengers tumble to the ground. When the witch suddenly finds herself face-to-face with a hungry dragon, her new friends must work together to come to her rescue.The story is filled with adventure and laced with humour. ‘Room on the Broom’ celebrates kindness, inclusion and the power of friendship. Julia Donaldson’s playful rhymes add to the beauty of the story.Kate Winslet knows the bookWinslet knows the book well. She has read it to all her children. The fun, adventure and warmth that Winslet’s voice brings to the story are not entirely accidental. “I have read this book to all of my children, and it’s from the same author as ‘The Gruffalo’ and the same illustrator as ‘The Gruffalo’, and the same author and illustrator, too, as ‘The Smartest Giant in Town’. I really love being able to go into the worlds of these authors because they are imaginative. They are fun. There are always lots of characters. And as a person who loves reading stories to children, there are always lots of fun and silly voices to do,” Winslet said in a statement. Her performance leans into those voices, giving each animal its own personality as the witch’s journey gets busier and noisier. All these elements also make the book a perfect fit for the Halloween season.The SAG-AFTRA Foundation sees the book’s staying power as part of its appeal. Courtney B. Vance, President and Chairman of the Foundation, pointed to the lasting message beneath the spells and flying: “Room on the Broom has delighted children and families for 25 years because beneath all of the magic and adventure is a beautiful message about kindness, generosity and making room for others. Kate is an extraordinary storyteller, and we are thrilled to have her bring this beloved book to life for Storyline Online. It’s the perfect story to share with children, families and classrooms as we head into the Halloween season.”Storyline Online is produced by the nonprofit SAG-AFTRA Foundation and draws millions of views each month. Winslet’s reading is the 104th read-aloud in the library, which already includes performances by Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Viola Davis, Oprah Winfrey and Michelle Yeoh, among many others. Each video pairs an actor’s reading with illustrations created for the programme. Families and teachers can watch the video for free at StorylineOnline.net, where the full library is also available. The video also comes with a free activity guide aligned with Common Core Standards, designed to encourage reading comprehension and creative play in the classroom or at home.You use AI every day. articles.title: 3 held for wildlife hunting in Jaisalmer
articles.summary: Forest Department arrests 3 for alleged fox and rabbit hunting near Swangiya Mata Temple in Jaisalmer; animals died; case filed under Wildlife Act.
articles.body: Jaisalmer: The Forest Department has arrested three men for allegedly hunting wild animals, including a fox and a rabbit, near Swangiya Mata Temple in Gajroopsagar area of Kishanghat in Jaisalmer. Both animals were found in a semi-conscious condition and later died despite medical treatment.Three accused were arrested late Thursday evening after a tip-off about illegal hunting near a temple. A Forest Department team raided and cordoned off the area before apprehending them.On Friday, they were produced before a court, which remanded them to judicial custody.Jaisalmer Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Kumar Shubham said the department had received specific information that some people were hunting rare wildlife in Gajroopsagar area near Swangiya Mata Temple.Acting on the information, a team from the Jaisalmer Forest Range, under the supervision of Regional Forest Officer Shyam Sunder Nagora and Assistant Conservator of Forests Dilip Singh Rathore, raided the location and caught the suspects.The accused have been identified as Mularam, Uttamaram and Chandranath, all residents of Jaisalmer district.During the operation, the forest officials recovered a fox and a rabbit in a semi-conscious condition from their possession. Fox is listed under Schedule I and rabbit under the relevant protected schedule of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2022.Considering their critical condition, the animals were immediately shifted to a veterinary hospital for treatment. A medical team from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) was also called in to assist in their rescue and treatment. However, despite the efforts of the veterinary experts, both animals succumbed to their injuries and died during treatment.The Forest Department also seized a traditional wildlife trapping device known as 'Kud', other equipment allegedly used for hunting, and two motorcycles from the accused. A case has been registered against them under the relevant provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and they were questioned in detail.DFO Kumar Shubham said illegal hunting and wildlife crimes pose a serious threat to biodiversity and ecological balance.
